pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.3.2)
- B9.3.2.1 — Derive the formulas for determining the surface area of prisms (cuboid and triangular prism) and use them to solve problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- identify cuboids and triangular prisms and draw their nets
- find the surface area of a cuboid and of a triangular prism from their nets
- express points in the Cartesian plane as position vectors

pages.title: Prisms and their nets
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Identify cuboids and triangular prisms, draw their nets to construct the 3-D shapes, and use them to determine the surface area.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.2.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Prism** — A **prism** is a solid with two identical, parallel end faces (its **cross-section**) joined by rectangular faces. A **cuboid** has a rectangular cross-section (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices). A **triangular prism** has a triangular cross-section (5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices). A **net** is a flat shape that folds up to make the solid.
[[fig:m9-f24|Figure 10.1: A cuboid and a triangular prism]]
## ✏️ Example 10.1
Sort these into cuboids and triangular prisms: a matchbox, a Toblerone-style chocolate box, a brick, a tent with triangular ends, a shoe box, a roof ridge tile.
**Solution**
**Cuboids:** matchbox, brick, shoe box. **Triangular prisms:** the chocolate box, the tent, the ridge tile.
## ✏️ Example 10.2
Identify each net.
[[fig:m9-f25]]
Figure 10.2: Two nets
**Solution**
a) A net of a **cuboid** (six rectangles in three matching pairs).
b) A net of a **triangular prism** (two triangles and three rectangles).
> 🧪 **Activity 10.1 — Making and measuring nets**
1. Open out an empty cardboard box (a cuboid) and a triangular-prism package. Lay each flat — it is a net.
2. Measure each face and calculate its area. Add all the areas to get the **surface area**.
3. Draw your own net of a cuboid 5 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm on card, cut it out, add flaps, fold and glue it.

pages.title: Surface area of a cuboid
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the net of a cuboid to determine its surface area.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.2.1.2
[[fig:m9-f26|Figure 10.3: Net of a cuboid l × w × h]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Surface area of a cuboid** — A cuboid has three pairs of equal rectangular faces: l × w (top and bottom), l × h (front and back), w × h (two ends). **Surface area = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh = 2(lw + lh + wh)**. For a cube of edge a: **6a²**.
## ✏️ Example 10.3
Find the surface area of cuboids measuring a) 8 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm b) a cube of edge 4.5 cm c) a closed box 1.2 m × 80 cm × 50 cm (in m²).
**Solution**
a) 2(8 × 5 + 8 × 3 + 5 × 3) = 2(40 + 24 + 15) = 2 × 79 = **158 cm²**
b) 6 × 4.5² = 6 × 20.25 = **121.5 cm²**
c) In metres: 1.2 × 0.8 × 0.5. SA = 2(0.96 + 0.6 + 0.4) = 2 × 1.96 = **3.92 m²**
## ✏️ Example 10.4
An open water tank (no lid) is 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1 m high. Find the area of metal sheet used to make it.
**Solution**
Without the top: area = lw + 2lh + 2wh = 3 + 4 + 3 = **10 m²**
> ✏️ **Practice:** Exercise 10.1, at the end of section 10.3, covers this section too. Tap **Quick check** to try its questions.

pages.title: Surface area of a triangular prism
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use the net of a triangular prism to determine its surface area.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.2.1.3
[[fig:m9-f27|Figure 10.4: Net of a triangular prism]]
> 🔑 **Key idea: Surface area of a triangular prism** — Surface area = 2 × (area of the triangular end) + (sum of the areas of the three rectangles). The three rectangles together form one long rectangle: **perimeter of triangle × length of prism**. So **SA = 2 ×** [[1/2]]**bh + (a + b + c) × l**.
## ✏️ Example 10.5
Find the surface area of a triangular prism whose cross-section is a right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, and whose length is 15 cm.
**Solution**
Two triangles: 2 × [[1/2]] × 6 × 8 = 48 cm².
Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 15 = 24 × 15 = 360 cm².
Surface area = 48 + 360 = **408 cm²**
## ✏️ Example 10.6
A tent is a triangular prism. Its ends are isosceles triangles with base 3 m and sloping sides 2.5 m; it is 4 m long and has a groundsheet. Find the area of canvas needed (including the groundsheet).
**Solution**
Height of the triangle = √(2.5² − 1.5²) = √4 = 2 m. Two ends: 2 × [[1/2]] × 3 × 2 = 6 m².
Rectangles: (2.5 + 2.5 + 3) × 4 = 32 m².
Canvas = 6 + 32 = **38 m²**

pages.title: Position vectors
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Express points in the Cartesian plane as position vectors.
Curriculum indicator B9.3.2.1.4
> 🔑 **Key idea: Position vector** — The **position vector** of a point P(x, y) is the vector vec{OP} from the **origin O(0, 0)** to P: vec{OP} = col{x;y}. It describes exactly where P is.
## ✏️ Example 10.7
a) Identify the origin and the position vector of P in the diagram. b) Draw and write the position vectors of M(2, 3) and N(−1, 2).
[[fig:m9-f28]]
Figure 10.5: Position vectors from the origin
**Solution**
a) The origin is **O(0, 0)**, where the axes cross. P is at (4, 1), so vec{OP} **=** col{4;1}.
b) vec{OM} **=** col{2;3} and vec{ON} **=** col{−1;2}.
For any two points, vec{MN} = vec{ON} − vec{OM} = col{−1 − 2;2 − 3} = col{−3;−1}.

pages.title: Exercise 10.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 10.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Write the position vectors of A(5, −2), B(−3, −4) and C(0, 6).
2. The position vector of Q is col{−4;7}. Write the coordinates of Q.
3. Given vec{OA} = col{2;5} and vec{OB} = col{6;−1}, find vec{AB} and |vec{AB}|.

pages.title: Chapter 10 summary
pages.body:
- Cuboid: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh); cube: 6a².
- Triangular prism: SA = 2 × triangle area + perimeter of triangle × length.
- Position vector of P(x, y) is vec{OP} = col{x;y}; vec{AB} = vec{OB} − vec{OA}.
